description: pkix-chain/src/lib.rs:1235-1279: verify_ocsp_responder takes `issuer: &Certificate` AND `chain: &[Certificate]`. The two arguments must be consistent (chain[0].issuer matches issuer.subject by DN, AND ideally issuer is in the chain so verify_chain's signature check covers it) but the function does NOT enforce that issuer is in chain. The rustdoc at lines 1286-1290 hand-waves: 'The cryptographic signature check ... is already covered by verify_chain when issuer appears in the chain.' But the function doesn't VERIFY that issuer appears in chain — a caller can pass a completely orphan `issuer` cert that DN-matches chain[0].issuer without ever being in the chain or anchors. Then the wrapper returns Ok even though the supposed-issuer never signed anything. This is closely related to PKIX-q9hv.3 (DN-match insufficient). Two layers of fix: (a) the spec-correct delegation pinning per PKIX-q9hv.3, AND (b) enforce that `issuer` either appears in chain (by content equality) or is the trust anchor that terminated the path. Otherwise the issuer argument is API-level theater.
title: verify_ocsp_responder takes &Certificate for issuer but doesn't enforce that it's in the chain
